de18_team.topic: DOGE operators: leaders, engineers, records examined, recruiting, vetting, where they went

claims.text: Steve Davis: joined SpaceX in 2003 as about its 14th hire; led the Boring Company from 2018 (president); ran cost-cutting at X after the 2022 acquisition; NYT described him as 'effectively the leader of DOGE'; ProPublica/Independent: ran day-to-day operations; led the 'Fork in the Road' email; left at end of May 2025; Politico (July 2025) reported continued influence after leaving

Davis ran DOGE's day-to-day operations including hiring and firing (WSJ); as an SGE he kept his job as Boring Company CEO; White House announced his exit the day after Musk announced his (29 May 2025); Katie Miller reportedly left to work for Musk; Leavitt: 'Surely, the mission of DOGE will continue'

Tom Krause, a DOGE deputy and CEO of Cloud Software Group, performing duties of Treasury fiscal assistant secretary on an acting basis, keeping his CEO job as an SGE; replaced David Lebryk, top career official who retired after a clash with Musk allies over payment-system access; Treasury said DOGE had 'read-only access'; systems handle more than $6 trillion a year

Bloomberg 10 Mar 2025: DOGE sent Antonio Gracias (Valor Equity Partners; former Tesla board member and early SpaceX investor), Scott Coulter (formerly Lone Pine Capital) and Michael Russo (formerly Shift4) to the Social Security Administration

Thomas Shedd: about eight years at Tesla as engineer/software developer; appointed director of GSA's Technology Transformation Services in January 2025; outlined an 'AI-first' strategy in early February 2025 (Wired, 404 Media); 18F eliminated (NYT, 3 Mar 2025); also Labor Department CIO (Nextgov, March 2025); replaced at TTS February 2026 and named senior adviser for fraud prevention at GSA; on unpaid leave from Tesla, which ethics experts called unusual

Reuters 31 Jan 2025: at OPM, Amanda Scales, a former Musk employee, was chief of staff; Brian Bjelde, at SpaceX since 2003 and its VP of human resources, and Riccardo Biasini, former Tesla engineer and Boring Company director, were senior advisers; Musk aides revoked some senior career staff's access to OPM data systems including EHRI; an official: 'There is no oversight'

Wired (2 Feb 2025) named six engineers aged 19–24: Akash Bobba (UC Berkeley M.E.T.; internships at Bridgewater, Meta, Palantir; OPM 'expert'), Edward Coristine (recent high-school graduate, Northeastern, briefly at Neuralink; OPM 'expert'), Luke Farritor (dropped out of Nebraska; SpaceX intern; Thiel fellow; GSA email), Gautier Cole Killian (McGill; Jump Trading; DOGE volunteer), Gavin Kliger (Berkeley; Databricks; special adviser to OPM director per LinkedIn), Ethan Shaotran (Harvard; founder of Energize AI; second in a Musk-company-sponsored hackathon; GSA email); Trump: 'They're very smart, though, Peter. They're like you'; White House: 'in full compliance with federal law'
Farritor, 23 per Wired's sources, co-awarded $700,000 in the 2024 Vesuvius Challenge for decoding a Herculaneum scroll; a current Thiel Foundation fellow; former SpaceX engineering intern

Marko Elez, 25: WSJ linked him to an account that said its owner worked at SpaceX and Starlink and posted 'Just for the record, I was racist before it was cool', 'You could not pay me to marry outside of my ethnicity', 'Normalize Indian hate' (NBC did not verify); resigned 6 Feb 2025; Vance: 'So I say bring him back'; Musk: 'To err is human, to forgive divine'; Trump: 'I'm with the vice president'

Bloomberg 15 Mar 2025: Elez briefly had read-write access though the court had been told read-only; Treasury forensics found no changes; he emailed a spreadsheet with names, transaction types and payment amounts to two GSA officials, unencrypted and without approval, breaching BFS policy (discovered after he resigned); BFS privacy officer called names 'low-risk PII'; he was rehired by DOGE at SSA, one of 10 DOGE staffers there

GAO-26-108131 (28 Apr 2026): one Treasury DOGE employee had access to three BFS payment systems Jan–Feb 2025, inadvertently given temporary create/modify/delete access in one, no evidence data changed; BFS did not ensure the employee agreed to IT rules of behavior before receiving a laptop; unencrypted payment information sent to another agency's DOGE team undetected by data-loss tools; BFS fully implemented 5 of 14 controls; six recommendations open

Coristine, 19: per Bloomberg, terminated from a brief Path Network internship in June 2022 'for leaking internal information to the competitors' after an internal investigation; he said in Discord posts he had done 'nothing contractually wrong'

Coristine listed as senior adviser at State and at CISA (Reuters), linked to DHS (WaPo), OPM 'expert' (Wired); nicknamed 'Big Balls'; Reuters (26 Mar 2025): EGodly, a group an FBI agent said was investigated in connection with swatting, thanked DiamondCDN, a company Coristine ran, for DDoS protection in February 2023; Coristine and State did not reply

Coristine was assaulted about 3 a.m. Sunday 3 Aug 2025 in Logan Circle in an attempted carjacking by a group of teens; two 15-year-olds arrested; Trump: 'If D.C. doesn't get its act together, and quickly, we will have no choice but to take Federal control of the City'

Kliger, 25, oversaw CFPB layoffs per court records (an employee's sworn declaration said he 'managed' firings of about 90% of staff); his public disclosure listed Tesla $100,000–$250,000, Apple $15,000–$50,000, bitcoin $15,000–$50,000, Solana $1,000–$15,000 — Tesla and Apple on the CFPB prohibited list; White House said Kliger 'did not even manage' the layoffs, calling the account 'an outright lie', and cited a 90-day divestment deadline of 8 May
Kliger and Sam Corcos (CEO of Levels) organized an IRS hackathon in April 2025 to build a 'mega API'; Corcos: 'one new API to rule them all'; Palantir 'consistently' mentioned as a candidate vendor

Anthony Jancso, former Palantir employee and co-founder of Accelerate SF, brought on by Steve Davis, wrote in a Palantir alumni chat: 'I'm helping Elon's team find tech talent for the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in the new admin'; 26 Nov 2024 post sought 'hardcore engineers'; recruiters posted in chat groups tied to SpaceX interns and former Palantir employees; six-month DC roles

Justin Fox and Nate Cavanaugh, with tech/finance backgrounds and no prior government service, used ChatGPT to flag NEH grants as DEI (more than $100M cancelled); Cavanaugh, asked if they reduced the deficit: 'No, we didn't'; Fox on a Holocaust survivors documentary: 'It's a gender-based story that's inherently discriminatory to focus on this specific group'

GAO-26-108192 (29 Sep 2026): for DOGE teams, only SEC documented background investigations (one underway, one from 2017 not confirmed adjudicated); CFPB and Education gave none; training documentation limited; 'Congress and the public lack assurance that this team member met relevant security requirements'; DOGE teams at four agencies had access to more than 23 systems
